s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of upper gastrointestinal bleeding with epigastric pain
salient_findings: Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration
key_facts: One-week history of epigastric pain and hematemesis
No significant medical or surgical history
Hemoglobin rose to 10 g/dL after transfusion
Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa
Well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass measuring 6×5 cm with fat attenuation

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST)
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration and a well-defined, heterogeneous mass with fat attenuation

shortlist.label: Peptic ulcer disease
shortlist.why_kept: Epigastric pain and hematemesis with a submucosal lesion and ulceration in the gastric antrum

shortlist.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding and a mass in the pre-pyloric region, although biopsy showed no malignant features

shortlist.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of upper gastrointestinal bleeding with a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with a well-defined, heterogeneous mass

raw.rationale: The presence of a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa and a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation on CT is most consistent with a GIST, especially given the lack of malignant features on biopsy which can sometimes be seen in GISTs

rejected.label: Peptic ulcer disease
rejected.why: While peptic ulcer disease can cause epigastric pain and hematemesis, the presence of a submucosal lesion and a well-defined mass is not typical

rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The biopsy showed no malignant features, making gastric adenocarcinoma less likely

rejected.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
rejected.why: Dieulafoy's lesion typically presents with a small, bleeding mucosal defect without a significant mass, which does not match the described submucosal lesion and mass

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: While leiomyoma can present as a submucosal lesion, the presence of fat attenuation in the mass on CT is more suggestive of a GIST
